classes.name: FairCurve_Batten
classes.summary: Constructs curves with a constant or linearly increasing section to be used in the design of wooden or plastic battens. These curves are two-dimensional, and simulate physical splines or battens.

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.signature: (P1: gp_Pnt2d, P2: gp_Pnt2d, Height: number, Slope?: number)
constructors.comment:
Constructor with the two points and the geometrical characteristics of the batten (elastic beam) Height is the height of the deformation, and Slope is the slope value, initialized at 0. The user can then supply the desired slope value by the method, SetSlope. Other parameters are initialized as follow :
- FreeSliding = False
- ConstraintOrder1 = 1
- ConstraintOrder2 = 1
- Angle1 = 0
- Angle2 = 0
- SlidingFactor = 1 Exceptions NegativeValue if Height is less than or equal to 0. NullValue if the distance between P1 and P2 is less than or equal to the tolerance value for distance in `Precision::Confusion`: P1.IsEqual(P2, Precision::Confusion()). The function `gp_Pnt2d::IsEqual` tests to see if this is the case.

instanceMethods.name: SetFreeSliding
instanceMethods.comment: Freesliding is initialized with the default setting false. When Freesliding is set to true and, as a result, sliding is free, the sliding factor is automatically computed to satisfy the equilibrium of the batten.

instanceMethods.name: SetConstraintOrder1
instanceMethods.comment:
Allows you to change the order of the constraint on the first point. ConstraintOrder has the default setting of 1. The following settings are available:
- 0-the curve must pass through a point
- 1-the curve must pass through a point and have a given tangent
- 2-the curve must pass through a point, have a given tangent and a given curvature. The third setting is only valid for {@link FairCurve_MinimalVariation | `FairCurve_MinimalVariation`} curves. These constraints, though geometric, represent the mechanical constraints due, for example, to the resistance of the material the actual physical batten is made of.

instanceMethods.name: SetConstraintOrder2
instanceMethods.comment:
Allows you to change the order of the constraint on the second point. ConstraintOrder is initialized with the default setting of 1. The following settings are available:
- 0-the curve must pass through a point
- 1-the curve must pass through a point and have a given tangent
- 2-the curve must pass through a point, have a given tangent and a given curvature. The third setting is only valid for {@link FairCurve_MinimalVariation | `FairCurve_MinimalVariation`} curves. These constraints, though geometric, represent the mechanical constraints due, for example, to the resistance of the material the actual physical batten is made of.

instanceMethods.name: SetP1
instanceMethods.comment: Allows you to change the location of the point, P1, and in doing so, modify the curve. Warning This method changes the angle as well as the point. Exceptions NullValue if the distance between P1 and P2 is less than or equal to the tolerance value for distance in `Precision::Confusion`: P1.IsEqual(P2, Precision::Confusion()). The function `gp_Pnt2d::IsEqual` tests to see if this is the case.

instanceMethods.name: SetP2
instanceMethods.comment: Allows you to change the location of the point, P1, and in doing so, modify the curve. Warning This method changes the angle as well as the point. Exceptions NullValue if the distance between P1 and P2 is less than or equal to the tolerance value for distance in `Precision::Confusion`: P1.IsEqual(P2, Precision::Confusion()). The function `gp_Pnt2d::IsEqual` tests to see if this is the case.

instanceMethods.name: SetAngle1
instanceMethods.comment: Allows you to change the angle Angle1 at the first point, P1. The default setting is 0.

instanceMethods.name: SetAngle2
instanceMethods.comment: Allows you to change the angle Angle2 at the second point, P2. The default setting is 0.

instanceMethods.name: SetHeight
instanceMethods.comment: Allows you to change the height of the deformation. Raises NegativeValue; - if Height <= 0 if Height <= 0.

instanceMethods.name: SetSlope
instanceMethods.comment: Allows you to set the slope value, Slope.

instanceMethods.name: SetSlidingFactor
instanceMethods.comment:
Allows you to change the ratio SlidingFactor. This compares the length of the batten and the reference length, which is, in turn, a function of the constraints. This modification has one of the following two effects:
- if you increase the value, it inflates the batten
- if you decrease the value, it flattens the batten. When sliding is free, the sliding factor is automatically computed to satisfy the equilibrium of the batten. When sliding is imposed, a value is required for the sliding factor. SlidingFactor is initialized with the default setting of 1.

instanceMethods.name: Compute
instanceMethods.signature: (Code: FairCurve_AnalysisCode, NbIterations: number, Tolerance: number): { returnValue: boolean; Code: FairCurve_AnalysisCode }
instanceMethods.comment:
Performs the algorithm, using the arguments Code, NbIterations and Tolerance and computes the curve with respect to the constraints. Code will have one of the following values:
- OK
- NotConverged
- InfiniteSliding
- NullHeight The parameters Tolerance and NbIterations control how precise the computation is, and how long it will take.
@returns A result object with fields:
- `returnValue`: the C++ return value
- `Code`: updated value from the call.

instanceMethods.name: SlidingOfReference
instanceMethods.comment: Computes the real number value for length Sliding of Reference for new constraints. If you want to give a specific length to a batten curve, use the following syntax: b.SetSlidingFactor(L / b.SlidingOfReference()) where b is the name of the batten curve object.

instanceMethods.name: GetFreeSliding
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the initial free sliding value, false by default. Free sliding is generally more aesthetically pleasing than constrained sliding. However, the computation can fail with values such as angles greater than PI/2. This is because the resulting batten length is theoretically infinite.

instanceMethods.name: GetConstraintOrder1
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the established first constraint order.

instanceMethods.name: GetConstraintOrder2
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the established second constraint order.

instanceMethods.name: GetP1
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the established location of the point P1.

instanceMethods.name: GetP2
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the established location of the point P2.

instanceMethods.name: GetAngle1
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the established first angle.

instanceMethods.name: GetAngle2
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the established second angle.

instanceMethods.name: GetHeight
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the thickness of the lathe.

instanceMethods.name: GetSlope
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the established slope value.

instanceMethods.name: GetSlidingFactor
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the initial sliding factor.

instanceMethods.name: Curve
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the computed curve a 2d BSpline.

classes.name: FairCurve_MinimalVariation
classes.summary: Computes a 2D curve using an algorithm which minimizes tension, sagging, and jerk energy. As in {@link FairCurve_Batten | `FairCurve_Batten`}, two reference points are used. Unlike that class, {@link FairCurve_MinimalVariation | `FairCurve_MinimalVariation`} requires curvature settings at the first and second reference points. These are defined by the rays of curvature desired at each point.

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.signature: (P1: gp_Pnt2d, P2: gp_Pnt2d, Heigth: number, Slope?: number, PhysicalRatio?: number)
constructors.comment:
Constructs the two contact points P1 and P2 and the geometrical characteristics of the batten (elastic beam) These include the real number values for height of deformation Height, slope value Slope, and kind of energy PhysicalRatio. The kinds of energy include:
- Jerk (0)
- Sagging (1). Note that the default setting for Physical Ration is in {@link FairCurve_Batten | `FairCurve_Batten`} Other parameters are initialized as follow :
- FreeSliding = False
- ConstraintOrder1 = 1
- ConstraintOrder2 = 1
- Angle1 = 0
- Angle2 = 0
- Curvature1 = 0
- Curvature2 = 0
- SlidingFactor = 1 Warning If PhysicalRatio equals 1, you cannot impose constraints on curvature. Exceptions NegativeValue if Height is less than or equal to 0. NullValue if the distance between P1 and P2 is less than or equal to the tolerance value for distance in `Precision::Confusion`: P1.IsEqual(P2, Precision::Confusion()). The function `gp_Pnt2d::IsEqual` tests to see if this is the case. Definition of the geometricals constraints

instanceMethods.name: SetCurvature1
instanceMethods.comment: Allows you to set a new constraint on curvature at the first point.

instanceMethods.name: SetCurvature2
instanceMethods.comment: Allows you to set a new constraint on curvature at the second point.

instanceMethods.name: SetPhysicalRatio
instanceMethods.comment: Allows you to set the physical ratio Ratio. The kinds of energy which you can specify include: 0 is only "Jerk" Energy 1 is only "Sagging" Energy like batten Warning: if Ratio is 1 it is impossible to impose curvature constraints. Raises DomainError if Ratio < 0 or Ratio > 1.

instanceMethods.name: Compute
instanceMethods.signature: (Code: FairCurve_AnalysisCode, NbIterations: number, Tolerance: number): { returnValue: boolean; Code: FairCurve_AnalysisCode }
instanceMethods.comment:
Computes the curve with respect to the constraints, NbIterations and Tolerance. The tolerance setting allows you to control the precision of computation, and the maximum number of iterations allows you to set a limit on computation time.
@returns A result object with fields:
- `returnValue`: the C++ return value
- `Code`: updated value from the call.

instanceMethods.name: GetCurvature1
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the first established curvature.

instanceMethods.name: GetCurvature2
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the second established curvature.

instanceMethods.name: GetPhysicalRatio
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the physical ratio, or kind of energy.

classes.name: FairCurve_Newton
classes.summary: Algorithm of Optimization used to make "FairCurve".

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.signature: (theFunction: math_MultipleVarFunctionWithHessian, theSpatialTolerance?: number, theCriteriumTolerance?: number, theNbIterations?: number, theConvexity?: number, theWithSingularity?: boolean)
constructors.comment: The tolerance required on the solution is given by Tolerance. Iteration are stopped if (!WithSingularity) and H(F(Xi)) is not definite positive (if the smaller eigenvalue of H < Convexity) or `IsConverged()` returns True for 2 successives Iterations. Warning: This constructor do not computation.

instanceMethods.name: IsConverged
instanceMethods.comment: This method is called at the end of each iteration to check the convergence: || Xi+1 - Xi || < SpatialTolerance/100 Or || Xi+1 - Xi || < SpatialTolerance and |F(Xi+1) - F(Xi)| < CriteriumTolerance * |F(xi)| It can be redefined in a sub-class to implement a specific test.
